{'text': 'Over the years, Apple has continued to add more customization options to iOS. Starting with the reintroduction of full Lock Screen personalization in iOS 16, followed by icon tinting in iOS 18, translucent icons in iOS 26, and now iOS 27 brings complete Liquid Glass sliders.', 'type': 'text'}

{'text': "The iPhone has become increasingly personalized over time, and that's a good thing. Now that we can tint the icons on the Home Screen, why not extend this feature to other parts of the operating system?", 'type': 'text'}

{'text': "Since iOS 27 hasn't been officially released to the public yet, what I'm discussing here about what the next version of Apple's system could do might be premature. However, I believe that adding themed app color schemes, beyond just light and dark modes, would be a logical next step.", 'type': 'text'}

{'text': "What I basically want is to recreate the Material You effect on iOS, but instead of being based on the wallpaper, it's based on the icon color—though Apple should also offer an option to match the wallpaper. Apple added a feature last year that lets icons match the color of the MagSafe case you're using, which would also pair perfectly with this themed color feature.", 'type': 'text'}

{'text': "It's also worth mentioning that Apple previously introduced color themes at this year's WWDC for Xcode, the integrated development environment they use to develop Apple software, featuring a wealth of attractive options—so why not bring this fun to the iPhone? Even the Mac, in its current state, allows you to set a system-wide color tone for third-party apps.", 'type': 'text'}

{'text': 'Summary', 'type': 'text'}

{'text': 'In summary, I think a themed color feature for iOS would look great and be another step toward greater personalization.', 'type': 'text'}

{'text': 'What are your thoughts on introducing themed colors to iOS and iPadOS? Feel free to let us know in the comments.', 'type': 'text'}
